_about: Public-domain William Clagett (1646-1688), preacher to Gray's Inn and a leading Anglican writer against Rome under James II, for the Word Hoard: his Paraphrase with Notes on John VI, The Religion of an Oath, Of the Humanity and Charity of Christians, two pieces from the 1688 Popery controversy that name him, and his collected sermons (Seventeen Sermons, Eleven Sermons, and the 1720 Sermons). Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-24 by lane A, round 138 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted. His many anonymous tracts against Dissent and against Popery, and the Discourse concerning the Operations of the Holy Spirit, are held until Adam rules on catalogue attributions.

clagett-humanity-charity: Of the humanity and charity of Christians. ...  1687 (catalogued 1687)
